about: El Niño pages update (26 November 2026): the latest official ENSO bulletins after the batch in research/2026-11/enso-asia, WHO's own El Niño documents, forecast products for the Heat Tool Finder, and Indian national guidance for the four protections on /el-nino-and-cities/. Sources were found by web search from the build session, which cannot open them, so every term is taken from the document's title or from wording search results quoted from it; a claim reaches a page only if the GitHub source check finds every term. This batch never replaces a claim confirmed in enso-asia: a page that does not open here leaves earlier verified content as it was.

claims.text: NOAA's archived copy of its 12 November 2026 discussion keeps the El Niño Advisory and the outlook of a strong-to-very strong El Niño likely through January-March 2027.
NOAA's weekly ENSO update, published between monthly discussions, keeps the El Niño Advisory; it is a weekly monitoring summary, not a new monthly outlook.
The Bureau of Meteorology reports a weekly relative Niño3.4 value of +2.67 °C for the week ending 22 November 2026, below the event's peak so far of +2.88 °C.
The Bureau says most models expect warming in the tropical Pacific to peak in December or January and to stay above El Niño thresholds into the southern autumn of 2027 (March to May 2027).
The Bureau notes that a strong Niño3.4 signal does not necessarily mean strong impacts.

The Bureau reports a weekly Indian Ocean Dipole index of +0.53 °C for the week ending 22 November 2026, and expects the positive Indian Ocean Dipole to weaken and return to neutral in early southern summer.

ASMC's El Niño page predicts the Relative Niño3.4 index to peak during November to December 2026, with most models predicting El Niño to begin weakening in January to February 2027 and strong El Niño conditions persisting until February to March 2027.
ASMC expects positive Indian Ocean Dipole conditions to weaken and return to neutral in January 2027.
IMD's latest ENSO and IOD update bulletin reports neutral Indian Ocean Dipole conditions and expects El Niño conditions to continue.
WMO's update of 20 November 2026 describes stepped-up support for El Niño preparedness and early action; it is a project update, not a new climate forecast.
WMO's State of the Climate press release describes El Niño as expected to become very strong, with the possibility of being among the strongest on record.
WMO's State of the Climate press release refers to WHO's response to El Niño's anticipated health impacts.
WHO's Strategic Preparedness and Response Plan for El Niño-related public health risks covers October 2026 to September 2027 and describes WHO's Grade 3 response.
WHO's Global Public Health Situation Analysis for El Niño 2026 sets out expected public health risks, including heat.
IMD publishes an extended range forecast covering the coming weeks.
NDMA's national heat wave guidelines include rescheduling working hours and providing drinking water for workers.
NDMA's national heat wave guidelines include measures for schools.
The Ministry of Labour and Employment has written to the States and Union Territories asking them to issue directions to employers and to spread information on protecting workers from extreme heat.
Its advisory of April 2026, as reported by All India Radio, urged rescheduling working hours away from peak heat, adequate drinking water and shaded rest areas.
India's National Action Plan on Heat Related Illnesses sets out health facility preparedness before, during and after the heat season.
NCDC's guidance on heat and pregnancy notes higher health risks from extreme heat for pregnant women and the fetus, and covers assessment and timely referral in health facilities.

The Ministry of Education's 2022 guidelines for schools in a heat wave include starting early and finishing before noon, holding assemblies in covered areas or classrooms, reminding pupils to drink water, and keeping ORS available.
Mahila Housing Trust's 2024 cool roof study looks at heat in homes in an informal settlement in Ahmedabad, including homes where women do paid work.
